definitions.meaning: A French form of the name Sergei, borne by Russians such as the impresario Diaghilev
a hard-wearing twilled cloth woven from worsted wool

explanation.surface: A description of cloth woven in Russia from worsted yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a man's name used by Russians (Serge Diaghilev) and a durable twilled woollen cloth.

clue.text: No extended stay for this baseball-player!

definitions.text: No extended stay for this baseball-player!

parts.words: No extended stay for this baseball-player!
parts.note: a stay that is not extended is a brief halt, and split that way the phrase names a fielder positioned between second and third base

explanation.surface: A ballplayer who never gets to linger anywhere for long.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielding position between second and third base in baseball, named as a brief halt.

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the two words are being rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: In April a woman sets about changing a tyre on her car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' looks like the motorist's job but is the anagram signal on APRIL and LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: A radial-ply is a type of tyre whose cord plies run at right angles to the tread.

indicators.note: mainly means most of a word is used, so its final letter is dropped here

parts.note: forward, as in a precocious or advanced child, means early

explanation.surface: A heading that is chiefly about moving ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' drops the last letter, Y, from EARLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble rank in the British peerage, so a title of nobility.

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed, that is down
Conservatives are the political right

explanation.surface: A true-blue Tory through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is also the Conservative party colour, which makes the surface read as a loyal Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean complete or utter, as in an outright refusal.

parts.note: high means intoxicated and a tar is a seaman, so the clue pictures an inebriated sailor alone out at sea, as in the old sea shanty

explanation.surface: Strong tobacco smoke lingering in the salty sea breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High tar' suggests cigarettes; read 'high' as intoxicated and 'tar' as a sailor. The shanty asks what shall we do with one.
explanation.definitionFit: High means intoxicated and a tar is a seaman, so a high tar is an inebriated seaman.

definitions.meaning: meat cooked very lightly so it is still red and bloody
uncommon, seldom found

explanation.surface: A mild British oath: something remarkably out of the ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: underdone, as a steak oozing red juice, and seldom seen or uncommon.

clue.text: Thalia, for example, the old bat

definitions.meaning: Thalia was one of the three Charites of Greek myth, goddesses of charm
W. G. ..., the great Victorian cricketer, a batsman of old

explanation.surface: Calling the Muse of comedy a crotchety old woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old bat' looks like an insult but means a famous cricket batsman of the past: W. G. Grace, the bearded Victorian star of English cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Thalia was one of the three Graces of myth, and W. G. Grace was the celebrated Victorian batsman.

clue.text: Decimal point can be imperfect in school

parts.note: decimal refers to the base ten
SE, south-east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A school pupil getting a decimal point wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: In grammar lessons the imperfect is one example of this verb form, alongside past and future.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperfect is one form of verb time taught in grammar classes, so it is an example of this.

definitions.meaning: peaceful arrangement, everything in its proper place
a sequence, one thing following another

explanation.surface: A musical term for a sequence of chords.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a calm, tidy state (law and this) and a sequence or arrangement in succession.

clue.text: French one bound to be up in the air

parts.note: un is French for one
bound, as in bound to happen, means sure

explanation.surface: A Frenchman fated to go flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Undecided or unresolved, an idiom for something not yet settled.

clue.text: Iceberg held as it breaks up and crosses the Thames

indicators.note: an iceberg breaking up falls apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An iceberg gripped as it breaks apart drifting down London's river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks up' scrambles ICEBERG HELD AS. The answer is a London bridge spanning the river between Chelsea and Battersea.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension bridge in west London that spans the river from Chelsea to Battersea.

clue.text: Late getting out for a duck?

indicators.note: getting out suggests the letters break loose from their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer out for no score, dismissed late in the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out for a duck' is cricket for dismissed without scoring, which disguises the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater dabbling waterfowl is a kind of wild duck.

clue.text: Sportsman going downhill with a highball, say…

definitions.meaning: someone descending a snowy slope on skis
in cricket, a mishit ball sent very high in the air

explanation.surface: A sportsman heading down the slope with a whisky cocktail in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highball' looks like a drink; in cricket a ball hit steeply upwards is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who descends snow slopes on skis, and a cricket term for a ball hit steeply upwards.

clue.text: … top tennis player, we hear is to give up

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament draw

explanation.surface: A leading tennis player is said to be about to concede.
explanation.walkthrough: A tennis seed is a player ranked to be kept apart in the draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender or relinquish, as territory is handed over.

parts.note: an instant is a moment, shortened to mo
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cup will be instant, tea or coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like instant coffee; it means a moment, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine variety of Arabian coffee named after a Yemeni port.

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word for ever

explanation.surface: A nation where one party is forever being toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns AY into YA, after LIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation on the Mediterranean, so a country.

clue.text: Sent, go to Capri for a break that is divine

indicators.note: a break here means the letters are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone packed off to Capri for a holiday that is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a break' looks like a holiday, but signals an anagram of SENT GO TO CAPRI. 'divine' is the verb, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To divine is to foretell or predict the future.

clue.text: One who acts routinely giving name to gold love-apple

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
love-apple is an old name for the tomato

explanation.surface: Someone giving a name to a golden tomato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love-apple' is an old word for the tomato; 'giving name to' puts N at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot or machine-like person who behaves mechanically, without thought.

clue.text: Calling up East, carry a case?

parts.note: the vocative is a grammatical case, used for addressing someone

explanation.surface: Phoning the East and asking someone to bring a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like luggage to carry; it is a grammatical case used for addressing someone. 'carry' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Summoning memories or images to mind; something that brings feelings to the surface.

parts.note: Psycho is the 1960 Alfred Hitchcock thriller

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it would sound when spoken

parts.note: an annalist writes yearly historical records

explanation.surface: Combining the names of a psychologist, a director and a historian.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone covers only the last part: ANNALIST sounds like ANALYST.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Jung was a Swiss founder of analytical psychology, an example of such a therapist.

definitions.meaning: a fine sheer fabric of linen or cotton
a mown stretch of turf in a garden

explanation.surface: Asking whether cotton grass, a sedge, is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Cotton grass is a moorland plant, which hides the two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a fine sheer linen or cotton cloth, and an area of mown turf.

definitions.meaning: of inferior rank or status
to look threatening, like a frowning sky

explanation.surface: A cheap second-rate weaving machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loom' looks like a weaving frame but is the verb, to scowl or threaten; pronounced to rhyme with 'flower' it is this sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: inferior in rank, and (rhyming with flower) to frown or threaten darkly.

indicators.note: on in a down clue means one piece is placed above the other

parts.note: to deck is to adorn, hang with decorations

explanation.surface: Women staging a walkout on board ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck but is the verb, to adorn or hang.
explanation.definitionFit: A resounding blow, a thump or whack.

definitions.meaning: to frown or scowl menacingly
a fierce dazzling light

explanation.surface: Telling someone to turn down the gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' rhymes with flower here: to scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a fierce angry stare, and a harsh dazzling brightness.

clue.text: Title of novel that takes me back to Mummy?

indicators.note: back means the word me is written backwards

parts.note: ma is a child's word for mother

explanation.surface: A book whose title brings me home to my mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME into EM; MA follows. The novel is by Jane Austen.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's 1815 novel takes its heroine's name as its title.

indicators.note: mad suggests disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Comparing a speedy bird with a mad March hare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad hare' recalls the March hare; 'mad' scrambles HARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless South American runner like a small ostrich.

definitions.meaning: a regiment's colours are its banner
to droop or tire, lose energy

explanation.surface: Asking whether dyes will wash out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colours' looks like hues but is a military banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a banner or standard, and to weaken or wilt.

definitions.meaning: came safely through hardship
worn and toughened by exposure to the elements

explanation.surface: Wood that has lasted through the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: survived a crisis, and changed by long exposure to wind and rain.

clue.text: Heavy stick used in Ambala this year?

indicators.note: used in means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cudgel was used in an Indian city this year.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambala is a city in northern India; 'used in' finds the answer in AMBALA THIS. 'year' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian bamboo club bound with iron, used by police.

clue.text: Kit out mother with part in such a performance

parts.note: to rig out is to equip or dress
ma is a familiar word for mother
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: Dressing up mother for her role in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' is meant as a fuss, a tedious palaver, not a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winded, tiresome procedure; a palaver or fuss.

clue.text: Spirit released by a light rubber?

definitions.text: Spirit released by a light rubber?

parts.words: Spirit released by a light rubber?
parts.note: pictures the magic being freed from Aladdin's lamp when someone rubs it

explanation.surface: Something summoned out of a lamp by rubbing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A magic spirit of Arabian tales, freed from a lamp by Aladdin's rubbing.
